title: Resilient kernel routing for mixed-sku clusters with clock contention mitigation
creator: Aisha K. Patel
description: We observe tail latency spikes and throughput drops when mixed-sku nodes (H100/L40S/A10) share MIG-partitioned hosts under fluctuating clock governors. Current kernel selection prioritizes theoretical kernel throughput without factoring in dynamic clock throttling, MIG fragmentation, or prefill/decode phase sensitivity. This ticket implements a resilient kernel routing layer that incorporates live clock telemetry and phase-aware prefilling decisions to reduce 99th percentile latency under contention and avoid expensive kernel fallbacks during prefill->decode transitions.
motivation: Improve predictable latency and throughput when heterogeneous GPU SKUs coexist and when clock domains are unstable (thermal throttling, NVLink bandwidth shifts, or cloud provider clock scaling). Prevent user-visible regressions when prefill work is scheduled onto a slice whose clock is being reduced mid-request.
technical_design: 1) Collect and surface per-slice telemetry: current SM clock, memory clock, power_draw, MIG occupancy, and recent kernel runtime variance. 2) Add a lightweight kernel_ranking_service inside the runtime: it computes a dynamic score per kernel candidate using static model fingerprints (sequence_length, batch_size, kv-cache size) and live telemetry. Score components: estimated cycles (static), clock_factor (current_clock / sku_max_clock), contention_penalty (recent queue_delay percentile), frag_penalty (if MIG fragmentation reduces contiguous resources). 3) Phase-aware scheduling: mark requests as PREFILL or DECODE at admission. For PREFILL, prefer kernels and slices with higher clock_factor and lower frag_penalty; for DECODE, prefer latency-optimized kernels, but include a hysteresis window so PREFILL->DECODE switch doesn't cause a kernel swap unless score delta > threshold. 4) Clock contention mitigation: when a slice's clock_factor drops below a low threshold, the routing layer proactively shifts new PREFILLs to healthier slices and enables conservative fallback kernels for in-flight DECODEs only if predicted latency SLA will be missed. 5) Integration: expose tunables via /runtime/config (score weights, hysteresis, thresholds) and add tracing tags for decision reasons. 6) Implementation language: C++ core changes with a small Rust telemetry consumer (already used in infra) for safe ingestion. 7) Backpressure: add a soft-queue-limit per slice to prevent overloading a high-clock slice during bursts.
tasks: T1: Define score formula and default weight values (ENG experiment doc)
T2: Implement telemetry collectors for per-slice clock/power/MIG occupancy (C++)
T3: Implement kernel_ranking_service and expose simple API to scheduler
T4: Phase tagging propagation in API layer (PREFILL/DECODE)
T5: Hysteresis and threshold logic + config knobs
T6: Add unit tests and microbench harness for offline scoring validation
T7: Hardware lab validation across H100/L40S/A10 with mixed MIGs
T8: Rollout plan and gradual canary on runtime-1.22
T9: Docs and runtime console config UI hooks
acceptance_criteria: 99th-percentile latency for mixed-sku prefill+decode workload reduced by >=15% vs baseline on our lab trace
Sustained throughput (tokens/sec per GPU) is not reduced by more than 5% on average across H100/L40S/A10 when score weights are default
No incorrect kernel swaps mid-decode observed in end-to-end QA (zero user-visible decode corruption)
Config knobs allow ops to relax thresholds at runtime without restart
New telemetry fields (clock_factor, frag_penalty, decision_reason) appear in traces and dashboards
testing_plan: Unit tests for score calculation with synthetic telemetry vectors
Microbench: replay recorded traces from prod-mixed-sku lab and compare routing decisions
Hardware matrix: run prefills and decodes on H100/L40S/A10 in isolation and mixed with varying MIG partitions and induced clock throttling
Canary rollout: 1% of traffic on runtime-1.22 with aggressive telemetry logging, expand to 25% after 48h SLO checks
Chaos tests: force clock drop on a slice mid-request and assert graceful fallbacks
rollout_plan: Phase 0: internal lab validation on dedicated cluster (2w). Phase 1: Canary on internal staging (1%), monitor SLOs and traces (48h). Phase 2: Canary to small customer cohort and Dedicated nodes (10-25%) with toggleable score_weights. Phase 3: Global rollout with default weights and ops runbook for reverting. Rollback path: set score_weights to conservative values or disable kernel_ranking_service.
risks: Incorrect score calibration could steer too much load to fewer slices and create hot spots
Telemetry delays could make routing decisions stale; need bounded staleness handling
Complexity increases scheduler latency; must keep ranking computation sub-microsecond on admission path
Cross-sku pricing/regulatory considerations when moving work between customer-dedicated SKUs
notes: Related experiment: internal perf-run 2025-01-12 showed 23% p99 spike when L40S nodes joined H100 pool under thermal events
